newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak SAX index firms slightly on Nafta gains.
newsitem.headline: Slovak SAX index firms slightly on Nafta gains.

text.p: Leading Slovak shares closed mixed in quiet trading on the Bratislava Stock Exchange (BSE) on Wednesday, with gains to oil and gas storage company Nafta pushing the SAX index up 0.93 points to 198.58.
Brokers said the market remained flat but foresaw a possible revival of trading at the end of month.
"The only significant gains on Wednesday, those to the Nafta share, were only based on a settlement of a previous block deal," Dusan Sykora of ING Barings said.
Nafta traded 24,700 shares, closing up 50 crowns at 1,900 crowns, but Sykora said he did not expect this volume of trading to be repeated in the near future.
"The price of this deal, 1,900, was quite correct, but currently the spread between the demanded and offered prices in Nafta is too wide to allow such a (high volume) transfer," he said.
Steel maker VSZ closed unchanged at 605 crowns, on volume of only 46 shares, with Sykora saying the issue should revive soon.
